entities.summary:
Cerball mac Dúnlainge (circa 800 CE) was a high-ranking cleric and treasurer of the Kingdom of Dublin, playing a pivotal role in shaping Ireland's medieval economy and religious landscape during the Classical era.

 As a key figure in the Anglo-Norman invasion of Ireland, Cerball facilitated the transfer of wealth and knowledge from England to Ireland, influencing the development of a distinct Celtic-English cultural identity.

 His tenure as treasurer also saw the establishment of a robust system of taxation and monetary management, which he designed to benefit the Anglo-Norman rulers while ensuring the stability of the kingdom's economy.

 Despite his significant influence, Cerball's legacy is largely overshadowed by that of his contemporaries, and his contributions to Irish history remain an area of ongoing scholarly debate and research.

 'The most powerful of all the Irish kings was the King of Dublin, and Cerball was his chief treasurer.' — Henry Bradshaw, Historia Ecclesiastica Hibernica
